title: Red Snapper Pasta with Non-Dairy Tomato Sauce

steps.text: Core and dice the 2.76 lb tomatoes. Skins on is fine — they soften into the sauce.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Don’t add the pasta yet.
In a wide pan, heat the 4 tbsp olive oil over medium. Add the onion and cook about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the 4 minced garlic cloves and ½ tsp red pepper flakes. Stir constantly, about 45 seconds — garlic burns fast.
Add the diced tomatoes. Stir, then pour in the ½ cup Pinot Grigio to deglaze.
Add the 1 cup chicken broth, 1 tsp salt, and ½ tsp pepper. Simmer uncovered about 20 minutes, breaking up tomatoes as they soften.
steps.donenessCue: Tomatoes broken down into a chunky sauce, no raw firmness left.

steps.text: About 10 minutes into the simmer, add the 12 oz pasta to the boiling water. Cook to al dente. Reserve ½ cup pasta water, then drain.
Pat the 1 lb snapper dry and season with the ¼ tsp salt. Sear in the 1 tbsp olive oil in a separate pan, skin-side down first, about 7 minutes total.
steps.donenessCue: Flakes easily, opaque all the way through.

steps.text: Stir the lemon zest and juice into the sauce. Taste and adjust salt.
Add the drained pasta to the sauce. Toss, loosening with reserved pasta water as needed.
Top the pasta with the snapper and scatter the 3 tbsp parsley over everything.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: More body without dairy: stir a spoonful of tomato paste in with the tomatoes.
Swap the chicken broth for fish or vegetable stock, and add ¼ cup torn basil.
storage: Sauce (without fish): fridge 3–4 days, or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat gently with a splash of water or stock.
